purpose: Freeze a bounded, reproducible evaluation of the March 7 first-party statement that the Strait of Hormuz cannot remain closed beyond three weeks because global recession begins to take hold and countries around the world put a stop to it.

first_party_source.title: The 3rd Week Is Critical
first_party_source.authorized_text: We know that the Strait of Hormuz simply cannot be closed beyond three weeks, thats when global recession begins to take hold and countries around the world put a stop to it.

claim_decomposition.meaning: Operational shipping disruption remains at closure-like severity through approximately three weeks from the observed closure onset.
Operational closure-like conditions cease soon after the three-week threshold.
Independent global macro evidence near or after the threshold shows a material deterioration toward recession, not merely higher prices or a single-country slowdown.
Multilateral or multi-country action materially ends or reverses closure-like conditions rather than merely discussing, pressuring, negotiating, or allowing isolated transits.

primary_clock.basis: Independent chronology identifies the onset of the war and near-halt/closure-like Hormuz shipping disruption beginning February 28.

sensitivity_clock.basis: Forecast publication date; retained because the source sentence does not explicitly name its closure-start anchor.

clock_policy.rule: The primary operational clock and publication-date sensitivity clock must both remain visible. No favorable result may be obtained by silently switching clocks after observing outcomes.

criteria: commercial transits at or below 10 percent of normal traffic, or
authoritative reporting describes the strait as closed, near standstill, near halt, or effectively blocked with only isolated/authorized crossings
effective_closure_operationalization.reopening_requirement: Sustained, broadly available commercial transit materially above closure-like levels. Announcements, conditional safe lanes, isolated permissions, or a few crossings do not by themselves satisfy reopening.
effective_closure_operationalization.anti_hindsight_rule: Do not redefine closure after observing the chronology.

macro_recession_operationalization.reason_for_bounded_definition: The source says global recession begins to take hold, which is softer than a completed global recession and does not name a metric.
required_evidence: independent global growth forecasts or nowcasts showing material conflict-linked deterioration
evidence that deterioration approaches a recognized global-recession range rather than only slower positive growth
global or broad multi-economy scope rather than a single-country recession

classification_rule.SUPPORTED: Independent contemporaneous evidence indicates the global economy has entered or is very near a recessionary regime attributable materially to the disruption.
classification_rule.PARTIAL_MIXED: Independent evidence shows substantial global growth deterioration and recession risk, but baseline global growth remains clearly positive or recession is confined to an adverse/severe scenario.
classification_rule.NOT_SUPPORTED: Independent evidence shows no material global growth deterioration or recession risk near the threshold.
classification_rule.UNRESOLVED_SOURCE_MEANING: The phrase begins to take hold cannot be mapped reproducibly to the available evidence without inventing a threshold.

qualifying: multi-country diplomatic agreement that materially restores broadly available transit
coordinated maritime/security action that materially restores broadly available transit
other independently verified collective action that ends closure-like conditions
nonqualifying_alone: temporary or conditional lanes while traffic remains closure-like
single-country action without evidence it materially ended the closure
